The raw request path is the root attacker input for the entire build flow: get_spec_from_request slices the provider spec out of request.path, the spec is tokenized/unquoted by providers into repo URL and ref, and those values reach the `git ls-remote` argv (repoproviders.py:487-488) and the repo2docker container argv (build.py:146-171, 343). 'tp' asserts the source role is real, not that a vulnerability is confirmed.

The spec slice itself: `spec = self.request.path[idx + len(prefix) + 1:]` returns the raw, un-unquoted spec (kept deliberately because tornado unquotes path captures). This is the exact value handed to provider construction and downstream command arguments.

Query argument build_token is client-controlled (tornado unquotes query arguments too). It is cryptographically verified with jwt.decode (HS256, audience = provider spec, server secret) inside check_build_token; no flow into command construction. Boundary source, authentication use.

get_provider instantiates the provider class with the attacker-controlled spec (`providers[provider_prefix](config=..., spec=spec)`); the returned object's fields (repo, unresolved_ref, namespace, user, gist_id) are derived from the spec. Taint step from request spec into the provider object; a wrapper, not an input boundary itself.

Provider accessor whose return value becomes Build.repo_url - the trailing repo2docker argv element (build.py:169) and, for GitRepoProvider, an argument of the git ls-remote command. The returned value is spec-derived (GitRepoProvider returns the unquoted arbitrary git URL; Zenodo/Figshare/Dataverse return the raw spec). Propagation step from provider to command parameters.

entries.rationale: Project wrapper that constructs and returns the complete repo2docker command list; the returned list embeds request-derived values: '--ref' (Build.ref), '--appendix' (Build.appendix), '--image' (Build.image_name) and the trailing repo_url. Marking the return value as a sink gives a precise intermediate alert point on the command payload itself.

The container args keyword receives get_cmd() and is the argv actually executed by the build pod; request-derived ref/appendix/image/repo_url are embedded as distinct argv elements. List-form (no shell), so the exposure class is argument injection (CWE-78 family) rather than shell injection. 'tp' asserts that this API genuinely is the pass-2 sink role - it does NOT assert a confirmed exploitable vulnerability (whether argument-level injection is exploitable depends on repo2docker's own argument handling). Normalized from the CSV keyword-encoding, see deviations.
